abstract_sentences.text: Auto-regressive speech–text models pre-trained on interleaved text tokens and discretized speech tokens demonstrate strong speech understanding and generation, yet remain substantially less compute-efficient than text LLMs, partly due to the much longer sequences of speech tokens relative to text.

evidence.anchor: longer sequences of speech tokens relative to text

abstract_sentences.text: This modality imbalance disproportionately allocates pre-training and inference compute to speech, potentially hindering effective cross-modal alignment and slowing performance scaling by orders of magnitude.
We introduce the Latent Speech-Text Transformer (LST), which aggregates speech tokens into latent speech patches that serve as higher-level autoregressive units.

evidence.anchor: aggregates speech tokens into latent speech patches

abstract_sentences.text: This design aligns the sequence-modeling granularity between speech and text while improving computational efficiency.

evidence.anchor: aligns the sequence-modeling granularity between speech and text

abstract_sentences.text: The resulting patches can align with textual units to facilitate cross-modal knowledge transfer and compactly capture recurring acoustic patterns such as silence.

evidence.anchor: capture recurring acoustic patterns such as silence

abstract_sentences.text: Across story-completion benchmarks under both compute-controlled and data-controlled settings, LST consistently improves speech accuracy while also improving text performance, achieving up to +6.5% absolute gain on speech HellaSwag in compute-controlled training (+5.3% in data-controlled training).

evidence.anchor: up to +6.5% absolute gain on speech HellaSwag

abstract_sentences.text: Under compute-controlled scaling from 420M to 1.8B parameters in a near compute-optimal regime, gains grow with scale, and improvements persist up to 7B parameters under fixed-token budgets.

These benefits extend to downstream tasks: LST stabilizes ASR adaptation and reduces the effective autoregressive sequence length during ASR and TTS inference, lowering computational cost without degrading reconstruction quality.
The code is available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/lst.

evidence.anchor: The code is available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/lst

introduction_moves.previous_question: How can text-LLM capabilities be approached for speech?
introduction_moves.answer: GSLM discretizes waveform speech and applies NTP, but the longer speech sequence creates data and inference burdens.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Recent work must exploit the larger text corpus while closing the speech/text gap.

evidence.anchor: up to three orders of magnitude more data

introduction_moves.previous_question: Have warm initialization, interleaving, and multi-stream modeling solved the gap?
introduction_moves.answer: They improve transfer but still leave a modality-performance gap on the same benchmarks.
introduction_moves.next_hook: A common cause of the remaining gap is needed.

evidence.anchor: gap between text-to-text and speech-to-speech performance

introduction_moves.previous_question: Why does cross-modal work still fall short of interchangeability?
introduction_moves.answer: The speech/text token-density mismatch is proposed as a primary alignment barrier.

introduction_moves.previous_question: How can the model process more semantic content at the same cost?
introduction_moves.answer: LST uses an encoder, global speech transformer, and decoder to operate on latent patches and reconstruct speech tokens.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Explain patch semantics, silence, and cross-modal alignment.

evidence.anchor: encoder that dynamically groups sequences of speech tokens

introduction_moves.previous_question: Does static compression suffice, and what does alignment cost?
introduction_moves.answer: Static patching gives an initial gain; word/subword alignment adds synchronization, while curriculum removes inference-time alignment dependence.

evidence.anchor: eliminate the need for such alignments during inference

introduction_moves.previous_question: Which testable promises follow from the preview?
introduction_moves.answer: The paper promises controlled-budget performance/efficiency, three patching analyses, and 1B–7B scaling.

introduction_moves.previous_question: How are the three promises related?
introduction_moves.answer: Granularity alignment is offered as the common mechanism.

related_work_moves.answer: The paragraph traces waveform generation, textless NLP, hierarchical AudioLM, interleaved SpiritLM/Moshi, and scaling-law work.
related_work_moves.next_hook: Move from speech-token history to textual transfer.

related_work_moves.previous_question: Which transfer routes compete with LST?
related_work_moves.answer: It contrasts initialization, interleaving, Chain-of-Modality, inner monologue, and parallel decoding, including latency trade-offs.

evidence.anchor: Transferring textual knowledge into speech LMs

related_work_moves.previous_question: What has been tried to reduce speech sequence cost?
related_work_moves.answer: Coarser units, hierarchy, parallel streams, acoustic BPE, and dynamic patching are grouped by compression and compute.
related_work_moves.next_hook: Connect dynamic patching to the proposed speech-text extension.

related_work_moves.previous_question: Which evaluations measure the claimed capability?
related_work_moves.answer: Zero Resource, sStoryCloze/TSC, and speech HellaSwag are positioned by lexical, syntactic, commonsense, and topic reasoning.
related_work_moves.next_hook: The appendix will test low-level lexical/syntactic preservation.

method_moves.previous_question: What is the conventional spoken-LM decomposition?
method_moves.answer: Speech tokenizer, decoder-only transformer, and vocoder define the baseline pipeline.
The model follows prior work with HuBERT semantic tokens from a 501-entry codebook at 25 Hz.

method_moves.previous_question: What objective does the baseline optimize?
method_moves.answer: Equation (1) gives corpus-level next-speech-token log likelihood.
method_moves.next_hook: Explain how interleaving bridges speech and text.

method_moves.previous_question: How are text and speech placed in one sequence?
method_moves.answer: Aligned text spans replace arbitrary speech spans with modality markers, allowing four input/output directions.
method_moves.next_hook: Introduce latent patching as the compression response.

evidence.anchor: allows the same model to be used for S→S, S→T, T→S and T→T tasks

method_moves.answer: The global transformer models patches instead of individual speech tokens, while local modules perform token↔patch transformation.

evidence.anchor: auto-regressively model latent patches of tokens

method_moves.answer: The encoder aggregates only speech spans into local patch representations and avoids hash embeddings.

evidence.anchor: sliding window self-attention and cross-attention layers

method_moves.answer: A lightweight decoder attends to generated patches/text plus a sliding 512-token local window for NTP.
method_moves.next_hook: Formalize X, Z, and patch indices.

evidence.anchor: cross-attention layers inserted between every transformer layer

method_moves.answer: Speech embeddings X, local index sets Pi, and latent sequence Z define the transformation.

evidence.anchor: maps X to a shorter sequence of patch embeddings Z

method_moves.answer: Non-overlapping segments of length p are encoded as one patch.
method_moves.next_hook: Use text-speech boundaries for semantic synchronization.

evidence.anchor: uniform compression ratio independent of alignment information

method_moves.answer: Wav2Vec2+CTC boundaries define word/BPE spans; out-of-span silence is separately patched, at the cost of an inference aligner.
method_moves.next_hook: Remove that deployment dependency with a curriculum.

evidence.anchor: one patch per text unit and silence segment

method_moves.previous_question: How is alignment supervision phased out?
method_moves.answer: Alignment is sampled with probability P(u), linearly decreasing from 1 to 0 across training phases.
method_moves.next_hook: Compare the strategies under controlled experiments.

method_moves.answer: Bounded-context aggregation is claimed to retain local discriminability while reducing redundancy.

evidence.anchor: preserving phonetic discriminability while reducing sequence-level redundancy

method_moves.previous_question: What prediction follows from the schedule?
method_moves.answer: Curriculum should retain alignment benefits while using static patches at inference.
method_moves.next_hook: Evaluate HellaSwag, SC/TSC, ASR, and TTS.

final_judgment.single_storyline: speech token 的高时间密度造成 speech/text 的 autoregressive 粒度不平衡；LST 用局部 latent patch 把 speech 压缩为更接近 text 的 unit，再由 decoder 做 token-level reconstruction。证据在 p.2「information-density mismatch」、p.4–5 组件和 p.7–8 controlled/scaling 结果。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留 Tables 3–4 的同预算主对照、Figure 4 的 scale 曲线、Table 5 的 ASR/TTS、Table 6 的 patching ablation 与 Figure 2 的架构图，直接回答性能、效率、scale 和迁移。证据：p.3、p.7–10。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: optimizer/hardware、完整架构、三次运行方差、speech ratio、BPE alignment、TTS 数据质量、低层 benchmark、token accounting 和 aligner noise 移入 A.1–A.11。方法基本自足，但真实时间效率、样本分母和部署边界仍需补证。证据：p.14–18「A.3–A.11」。
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 将 token→patch→token 变换具象化；Tables 3–4 共享 S→S/T→T 列结构并分离两种 budget；Figure 4 把跨规模趋势与 7B fixed-token 结果并列，形成短证据链。证据：p.3、p.7、p.5。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 效率主要用 token/context/generation units 与推导 FLOPs 表达，缺少 wall-clock；Table 6 的 approximately matched rows 仍混合长度与 alignment；TTS other CER 的方向差异被「matches」概括；Section 7 关于 downstream adaptation 的范围句与 p.8 fine-tuning 存在张力。证据：p.8、p.10、p.18。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 涉及 token/patch 粒度改变的论文，应把同预算主对照、压缩单元可视化、机制替代消融和尺度外推按一条因果链排列，并为每个收益绑定独立证据对象。本文的绑定点是 p.3–5 方法图与公式、p.7–8 主结果。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于存在 autoregressive compute 与多种预算的序列模型；若研究的是无序列成本的纯表示学习，或唯一 estimand 是真实系统 latency，则应以对应部署测量替代 token-level proxy。
